guide.title: Pediatric Cardiac Arrest & BLS
guide.lead: Children's hearts usually stop because they ran out of oxygen. Good ventilation matters as much as compressions. Know the ratios and depths, start CPR for a slow heart with poor perfusion, and dose everything by weight.

sections.title: Infant, child, adult
rows: Two thumbs encircling, or heel of one hand
notes: The two-finger technique is no longer recommended for infants.
Depth: at least one third of the chest depth.

sections.title: Slow heart with a pulse
sections.question: Heart rate below 60/min with poor perfusion despite good oxygenation and ventilation?
items: Poor perfusion: mottled or pale, cold, slow capillary refill, altered consciousness
sections.no: Keep ventilating with oxygen; monitor closely.

flashcards.question: Commonest cause of pediatric arrest
flashcards.answer: Respiratory failure and hypoxia, not a primary heart problem.

flashcards.question: Child compression depth
flashcards.answer: About 5 cm (2 inches): at least one third of the chest depth.

flashcards.question: Infant compression technique
flashcards.answer: Two thumbs encircling the chest, or the heel of one hand. The two-finger technique is no longer recommended.

flashcards.question: AED for a child under 8
flashcards.answer: Pediatric pads or attenuator if available; if not, a standard AED.

flashcards.question: When to start CPR with a pulse
flashcards.answer: Heart rate below 60/min with poor perfusion despite good oxygenation and ventilation.

flashcards.question: Pediatric epinephrine
flashcards.answer: 0.01 mg/kg IV/IO (0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL), maximum 1 mg, every 3–5 minutes.

critical.scenario: A 6-month-old is unresponsive and not breathing, with no pulse. Two EMS providers start CPR.
critical.question: Technique and ratio?

options.f: Two fingers is no longer recommended, and two rescuers use 15:2.

critical.scenario: A 3-year-old in respiratory distress goes limp. HR 40, mottled, no improvement despite good BVM ventilation with oxygen.
critical.question: Next step?

options.t: Keep ventilating and reassess in 2 minutes
options.f: A heart rate below 60 with poor perfusion needs CPR now.
Oxygen, ventilation and CPR come first.

critical.explanation: Heart rate below 60/min with poor perfusion despite adequate ventilation is treated as arrest.
